transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today? How can I help you?

I came in because I can’t get past this feeling—really this certainty—that I’m being punished for letting my father decline. My sister keeps showing me the doctor’s notes and telling me I did everything I could, that I didn’t do anything wrong, but it doesn’t change it. It feels like some kind of judgment has already been made against me.
Have you been feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things that happened with your father, even when others tell you you're not at fault?

Yes. I keep replaying everything—his appointments, what I should’ve pushed harder on, things I said or didn’t say. And then I think about arguments with relatives, and it all turns into me feeling like I was selfish… like I failed him.

It doesn’t really stop there either. I start thinking I’m useless at work too, like I can’t do anything right, and maybe I deserve whatever happens because of it.
Do you find that certain thoughts keep coming into your mind, even when you try not to think about them—like specific worries or images that are hard to let go of?

Yes. It’s mostly the same thoughts over and over. I keep going back over every decision I made about my father’s appointments, and every tense conversation I had with relatives. I try to stop, but it just loops, and I end up feeling like I was selfish… like I’m a bad daughter. Then it spreads to work too, like I’m useless there and deserve whatever happens to me.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive—like they come into your mind even when you don’t want them to—and do they cause you a lot of distress that’s hard to shake?

Yes. They come in even when I’m trying not to think about them. I’ll be doing something else and then I’m right back going over my father’s appointments, or a conversation with a relative, and I end up feeling like I was selfish. Like I’m a bad daughter.

And then it turns into feeling useless at work too, like I deserve whatever happens. It’s hard to shake once it starts.
When these thoughts come up, do you feel driven to do certain things—like checking, counting, or repeating actions—to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t really count or check things to make it stop. I mostly just get stuck thinking about it. I might go over it in my head again and again, but I’m not doing a specific action to prevent something from happening.
Have you felt down or lost interest in things you usually care about, like work or time with family and friends?

Yes. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It’s like the color has gone out of everything.

Even at work, sitting at my desk in HR, I just feel… disconnected from it. And things I used to care about, like being out in the garden, I can just stare at the beds and feel nothing really reaches me anymore.

latest_inference.note: This turn ruled out OCD (F42) as the primary concern since the patient does not engage in compulsive behaviors to alleviate anxiety. The differential remains narrowed to these conditions.
